answer: An escrow deposit on a public referral graph blocks fake-identity farms. Each identity posts 60 credits in escrow and names a sponsor; every edge is public. Two upheld disputes burn the deposit and slash its sponsor 30 credits. A lone account at its nadir draws disputes first, and a zephyr of cheap referrals fails because each sponsor backs at most three identities. The k-th fake still costs a fresh 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits, linear with no reuse. Honest agents reach the summit with one deposit, refunded after work. Failure mode: sponsor farming.
